1.explanation:
1. We launch a headless Chrome instance using chrome-launcher.  
2. We set Lighthouse’s settings to use throttlingMethod “simulate” along with explicit rttMs, throughputKbps, and cpuSlowdownMultiplier to match real-world conditions.  
3. We bump `maxWaitForLoad` and `maxWaitForFcp` to force Lighthouse to wait longer before closing out the simulation window, in an effort to capture late layout shifts.  
4. We run Lighthouse against the Venia bottoms page, extract the CLS and related performance metrics, and log them to the console.  
5. Finally, we kill the Chrome process.  

By comparing the CLS value here (usually 0) to a manual session in a real browser, you can see that Lighthouse’s simulate timing cuts off before late-arriving content has a chance to shift layout. This reproduces the bug where CLS is under-reported under simulate throttling.
1.bug_scenario: When you invoke Lighthouse on the PWA Venia bottoms page with throttlingMethod set to “simulate,” Lighthouse will use the lantern-based load simulator to throttle network and CPU, then stop the page evaluation as soon as the simulator thinks all work is done. On this particular page, however, images and add-to-cart overlays continue to load and shift content after Lighthouse’s simulation window closes, so Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) remains reported as 0 (see screenshot) even though the live page continues to shift.
